The exception is grain: the newer copy rewrote it to wrap on the torus, and the older per-pixel version draws a faint seam — it survives as grainPerPixel so the tool that already shipped textures made with it is unchanged. Proof: both regenerate byte-identical, kitten 8f275fa2 and counter-strike 4d513645. agents/tooling.md now carries the folder rule for tools.

what: the tooling shelf was a hand-kept array of two demo scripts while eight real tools sat beside them on disk. Its own guide said 'check tools.list before writing a new script', so an agent that did the right thing was told there was nothing there, and wrote its own copy of a generator that already existed. Nothing said a tool could be extended, or that reusable parts belong in a shared library.
fix: read tools/ off disk, list tools/lib/ by export, and say in the guide that improving a tool is the job

note: tools.list reads the directory now, so it cannot go stale: seven tools with their one-line summary taken from each file's opening comment, whether each exports main(), and every export tools/lib/ offers. It names any file with no description, the way plugin.sizes names a plugin with no guide. A registered tool that also turns up on disk is deduped by file. The guide says outright that a tool is yours to change, that anything reusable goes in tools/lib/, that you extract on the second copy rather than the third, and that a change is proved by regenerating and comparing bytes.

what: Assigned defect: automatic damage numbers are unreadable from kitten-survivors' play camera (follow distance 9, pitch -1.02, fov 50 — about 8.4 m of world per screen height, so a number is ~6% of the screen). The size is the builtin's SIZE = 0.55 at damage-numbers.js:42, and the automatic entity:hurt listener calls the module-local show() directly, so a game plugin has no seam: replacing context.damageNumbers.show does not reach it, the bus has no off or consume, and showing a second bigger number doubles every figure. The fix lives outside the lane's claimed files, so it is logged instead of made.
fix: Let the automatic number be tuned by the game: raise SIZE to ~1.0, or better, route the auto listener through context.damageNumbers.show and read defaults from a settable context.damageNumbers.defaults = { size, life, rise } so a hit-feel plugin owns the look in one place.

what: agent-runs/horde/measure-horde.mjs freezes at the first level-up: Choice Screen holds the clock, nothing picks a card, and every later minute re-reads the same frozen world at 0:23 — it printed 'min 10' rows that were really minute 0.4. Burned a full 10-minute sim run before noticing context.time was 22.8. Any critic numbers taken from it after the progression lane landed are fiction.
fix: Use agent-runs/horde/measure-density.mjs, which auto-picks a card and counts minutes by the engine clock, not loop iterations

what: A headless CLI call runs exactly one op, so 'simulate 60 then read horde.stats' cannot be done from the command line — every mid-run sample means writing a bespoke .mjs against startWorldInNode. A --then or a script op that chains ops in one world would have saved a scratch file per question.

Game Camera reads the level camera rule off disk asynchronously, so a one-shot headless simulate never sees it: the whole run plays behind the editor ortho view (snapshot says mode ortho mid-game) and anything measured from the play camera gets a fallback. The rule is already in memory as loadedLevel in start-world.js.
fix: Hand the camera rule to the plugin synchronously at level:loaded (expose loadedLevel.camera on the event or context) instead of re-reading levels/<name>.json

what: art-language.md section 4 pins the key light at about 34 degrees, but the east fence has a 3.6m hedge and 16m trees right behind it, and at 34 degrees they rake shadows metres into the play field. meadow.json now carries the key at about 60 degrees (its own rule: dusk is a colour decision, not a sun-angle one) and the doc disagrees with the meadow it describes.
fix: Update section 4: key direction [-0.47, -0.87, -0.17], about 60 degrees, and say why - tall things outside the fence set the floor for the key angle

what: meadow.json is generated, and this lane's claim covered the level file but not its generator - the camera block (pitch -1.05, distance 14, bounds 46.5) and key-light (direction [-0.47,-0.87,-0.17], at origin) fixes will be reverted by the next run of the tool.
fix: Mirror the meadow.json camera and key-light values into the generator before anyone re-runs it

note: damage numbers grew a live defaults object the game sets once; kitten-hit-feel sets size 1 for the 14m camera and the automatic listener follows
art-language section 4 now pins the key at 60 degrees and says why the fence line sets the floor
the generator now writes the proven camera and light; regenerating reproduces the lane's values byte-for-value
measure-density.mjs auto-picks cards and reads the engine clock; the frozen harness's numbers are labelled fiction

what: the lane brief said all four claimed files were NEW and 'the engine has no particle system', but plugins/builtin/particles.js existed at HEAD with 1003 lines and three plugins already calling context.particles. Half the reconnaissance budget went to discovering the brief's premise was false. docs/design.md still listed particles as a known gap, which corroborated the wrong premise.
fix: before fanning out, grep the branch for each claimed file and each claimed capability; a brief that says NEW must be checked against git, and a gap list must be pruned by whoever fills the gap

what: a kill in kitten-survivors now draws particles from three owners: Combat Effects fires 'blood' on entity:killed, Kitten Hit Feel fires 'sparks' on the same event, and Kitten Effects puffs fur on enemy:died. They read as one poof only because the palettes agree. Kill visuals need one owner; the particle calls in kitten-hit-feel.js belong in kitten-effects.js but that file was not this lane's to edit.
fix: move Kitten Hit Feel's define() recolours and its kill spark into Kitten Effects, leaving Hit Feel to weight, shake and sound only

what: npm test and npm run test:offline can never pass inside a lane worktree: the exit-code test expects 'snapshot --port 5999' to exit 2 (nothing to talk to), but in a worktree snapshot refuses with exit 1 because it would drive the main workspace's editor. Every lane that dutifully runs the packet's required checks burns time diagnosing a failure it cannot fix.
fix: make the test lane-aware, or give snapshot's lane refusal its own exit code the test accepts

note: the kernel hands the camera block over on level:loaded itself; the bus takes varargs and the plugin has nothing left to read

what: A lane cannot drive its own dev server: engine.mjs refuses every non-headless drive op from inside .agent-worktrees, even when the live editor on that port was started from the lane worktree with ENGINE_PROJECT and a private port. Verifying GLB models visually meant bypassing the CLI and calling window.engine from the browser.
fix: Let ping report the server's repo root and refuse only when it differs from the caller's, instead of treating every live editor as the main workspace.

what: Parallel lanes share one Chrome MCP tab group: mid-verification my tab was navigated from this lane's server on 5197 to another editor on 5180, and my next keyup/stop call landed on that other editor before I noticed the port change. Any lane driving a browser can silently hijack another lane's tab.
fix: Give each lane its own tab and check location.href before every driving call, or fold browser verification into the engine CLI so lanes never share a tab.

what: Model-built enemies never batch or instance: each GLB enemy is 2-4 primitives (one per material), and the horde caps at 600 alive, so the late game is ~1800 draw calls plus the shadow pass where the box meshes were 600. Fine today, but it is the first wall a full meadow will hit.
fix: Instance crowd families that share a model, or fail that, re-export the enemy GLBs as single primitives with vertex colours.

note: a lane may drive its own dev server with --port; every bridge reply names the checkout it serves and the CLI refuses a mismatch
cross-server landings are refused by the serves check; the shared-tab rule is written into agent-workspace.md and loop briefs

what: a lane started npm run dev with no ENGINE_PROJECT, so the server came up on the DEFAULT project - a counter-strike editor appeared mid-kitten-run on 5180, another lane's browser tab was navigated into it, and it outlived its lane. A bare dev server should say loudly which project it serves, and a gauntlet lane brief must pin ENGINE_PROJECT and the port

particles are invisible in the editor: frame-phase systems only run inside the play loop, and edit mode repaints through the shell's own draw path — so a burst fired from the terminal or console shows nothing until PLAY is pressed. Cost a long false hunt for a painter bug that was a dispatch rule. The old 1003-line particles.js had the same behaviour, unnoticed.
fix: run frame systems from the editor repaint too, or say in the loop's guide that 'frame' means play-mode frames only

note: the tab title now names the project it serves, and the loop-3 brief pins ENGINE_PROJECT and a port per lane
design.md's gap list no longer claims 3D model loading is missing, names the instancing cost, and records that frame systems draw only in play
recorded in design.md as a known gap: an effect can only be checked by pressing play
the lane guard now exempts --port and the serves check governs instead; test:offline passed 8/8 inside the loop2-effects worktree after merging mainline
reclassified: a defect of the game being built, not engine friction - carried to the loop-3 brief (kill visuals get one owner, Kitten Effects) instead of this ledger

what: Weapon upgrade cards are a placebo: kitten-upgrades grantWeapon calls context.weapons.upgrade/levelUp/grant/give but the weapons lane publishes context.autoWeapons and expects names like 'yarn ball', not ids like 'yarn-ball'. Nothing consumes 'kitten:upgraded' or entity.arsenal either. Found only by reading both files side by side after three in-game picks visibly did nothing.
fix: Wire grantWeapon to context.autoWeapons.upgrade with a card-id to weapon-name map, and add a check-time assertion when a granted weapon name is unknown

what: R-to-retry soft-locks after death: kitten-progression reloads the level, run-clock's watcher instantly re-ends the empty run at 0:00 and holds the loop, and the held loop never processes another R. The player is stuck on a zeroed death card. Cost the critic ~20 minutes to diagnose across two plugins.
fix: After loadLevel, runClock.reset() then begin() once play resumes; do not let the watcher end a run that never began

what: measure-density.mjs prints undefined stats: horde.stats' command handler became async (awaits camera.ruleRead) and engine.run returns its Promise unawaited, so stats.alive is undefined in every row. The loop-1 broken-harness failure mode recurred in the replacement harness.
fix: await engine.run('horde.stats') in harnesses, or make engine.run await command handlers

what: Live (non-headless) CLI 'run horde.stats' answers from the edit-mode world (time 0, born 0) while a run is playing in the browser, and the editor dropped from play mode to edit at least four times during an hour of critique (page reload or mode flip, no console trace survives). Live-run measurement is untrustworthy; headless plus in-page probes had to carry every number.
fix: Route live CLI ops at the play world when one exists, and log why play mode exits

what: Bridge broadcasts every op to all connected clients and keeps the first reply: a stale 328x202 automation tab from a dead job (.claude/jobs/41aae344 prof6) won every race, so bridged see.capture wrote a blank transparent PNG with confident marks and no hint which client answered. Cost half the test budget proving it. Replies should name their client (viewport, url, focus) and the CLI should let you pick or at least warn on multiple clients.
fix: include client identity in engine:reply, refuse or warn when more than one client answers, and have see.capture always renderer.draw() before copying the canvas so a throttled tab cannot return stale or blank pixels

note: the script op runs several ops in one headless world - simulate then describe then sketch is one CLI call

what: writeFrameFiles in engine/frame-sketch.js joins dirname(frame-sketch.js) with '../../agent-runs/see', which is one level above the checkout — headless see.sketch frames land in Z:/Code/agent-runs/see and the Tests panel's /agent-runs/see/<name>.png links 404
fix: join '../agent-runs/see' — frame-sketch.js is one level below the checkout root, not two

what: see.occlusion never uses the ID buffer: queries.js calls buffer.visibility(context, {of, rows, columns}) but id-buffer.js visibility(context, ids) takes an id array — the object is ignored, an array of every visible entity comes back, read.visibleFraction is undefined, and the verb always answers method 'rays', even in the browser
fix: call buffer.visibility(context, [entity.id]) and read the first element

note: writeFrameFiles resolves one level up from engine/, inside the checkout; strays recovered
queries calls visibility(context, [id]) and reads the per-id measure; proven in play - method id-buffer, 1390 pixels

what: browser-first agents never find the engine tooling: three fresh low-effort agents asked human questions and all went straight to Chrome screenshots (170KB a frame) and whole-page DOM reads - zero agent.context, zero see.* calls. The scent must reach the browser itself: a visually hidden machine-readable notice in the editor page that read_page and accessibility reads surface first, redirecting to agent.context
fix: one hidden DOM node in the shell naming the agent.context command

note: the shell carries the agent door: a hidden first link read_page surfaces naming agent.context and See, and the status bar says it visibly for screenshots

what: Queries answer from the live camera, but nothing but the mouse could aim it — an agent asking occlusion of an offscreen subject had no way to point the camera at it

note: see.view {"go":"name"} aims the live camera at a saved view; queries answer from it

what: Capture marks were numbered tags floating above entities — indistinguishable from the game's own damage numbers, and a reader cannot bind a floating number to the body below it
typeColour hashes two type names to the same hue — kitten and ground collide — so a marked thing can wear its backdrop's colour and vanish

note: Marks are hulls: each marked entity outlined in its type's colour on its own pixels, palette legend in the sidecar; marks:'tags' keeps the stamps; ui:false hides overlay sprites
describe nudges a marked type's hue 37 degrees at a time until it stands 25 degrees clear of every visible type; drawings read the palette

what: See's guide promises a sidecar 'marks' map that no sidecar carries; the mark number lives on each visible entry instead, so an agent following the instruction sheet looks up a key that is not there
fix: Say that each visible entry carries its own mark and hull, and that palette names the outline colour and never the thing's own colour

what: A cropped studio capture reports light.mean 10 of 100 because transparent background pixels are counted; the field that exists to stop an agent asking a vision model whether a frame is too dark would make it ask
fix: Measure brightness over the drawn pixels only, using the alpha channel or the ID buffer as the mask

what: An alone subject capture draws no hull though the guide says the subject is outlined white and wider, so a fresh agent bound the palette hex to the model's own material colour and called a pink-red 'warm brown'
fix: Either stroke the subject hull in the studio too, or state in the reply that a lone subject is unmarked and palette is not a material colour

what: startWorld calls loadPlugins() with no arguments, so the plugin finder has no loader to report to. A file that throws on import has no name and nothing to tell, so recording the failure needed a module-level side channel in loader.js that the finder writes to and the loader drains at boot.
fix: Call loadPlugins(loader) — or let a finder return {file, error} entries and have loader.add accept them — so a failed import is reported to the loader directly.

what: makeInspect is built at the very end of startWorld, after loadPlugins and loader.boot. Every error raised while the world is being built — a failed plugin import, a plugin whose onLoad threw, a missing startLevel — is emitted to a bus with no subscriber and logged through a console.error the patch has not replaced yet, so snapshot().errors was empty on a world that broke while starting.
fix: Create the log (or the whole inspect surface) before plugins are found, and hand it to the loader, so boot-time errors land in it as they happen instead of being read back out afterwards.

what: There are two findPlugins — one in engine/index.js for the browser, one in engine/start-world-node.mjs for node — and they are twins only by discipline. A rule about what happens to a file that will not import has to be written twice, in two files that different lanes own, so half the fix lands and the headless half stays silent.
fix: Put the shared half of finding plugins in one place (loader.js), leaving each half to supply only its import function, so a rule about failures is written once.

what: A headless script that ends in see.describe still pays for the simulate step's snapshot, which prints every one of the 842 entities in the level. Measuring one describe reply meant writing a wrapper that runs the CLI and throws the earlier replies away.
fix: simulate's reply should carry counts and byType, not the whole entity list — or script should answer only the last reply unless asked for all of them.

what: Headless, see.describe answers from the editor's orthographic camera even while a run is being simulated, so the frame holds scenery and no creatures. The guide says simulate brings a moment about, but never says the camera stays in the editor; the meadow's play camera only exists as a constant inside kitten-survivors/tests/see-battery.js, which is where I had to go and read it.
fix: Once a run is playing, headless context.view should follow the Game Camera the way the browser does — or see.view should ship a 'play' view and the guide should name it.

what: tests.run reports a red test with no way to tell whether it was already red before this lane touched anything. Proving the see-battery failure was pre-existing cost a git stash, a second full run, and a stash pop.
fix: Keep the last green result per test and say 'this was already failing at <commit>' beside a red one, or give tests.run a --baseline flag that runs the suite against HEAD.

what: Correction to p146: the Test Runner lives at plugins/builtin/tests.js, not test-runner.js.
fix: See p146 — a red result should say whether it was already red at HEAD.

what: git stash is shared by every worktree of one repository, so a lane that stashes to compare against HEAD can have its stash popped into a SIBLING lane's tree. It happened to me: my describe.js change vanished and another lane's see.js + queries.js changes appeared in my worktree instead. I had to save their diff, reset my tree, and retype my own change from context. The safe comparison is 'git show HEAD~1:<path> > <path>', measure, 'git checkout HEAD -- <path>' — no stash.
fix: agent.context and the worktree onboarding must forbid git stash in a lane and name the git show route instead; agent.release could refuse while the repo's stash stack is non-empty.

what: A lane worktree is created with no node_modules, so npm run test:offline and npm run dev both fail until you work out that dependencies were never installed. The headless world test fails on a missing 'three' and reads like broken engine code.
fix: agent.prepare should install or link node_modules into the new worktree, or the prepared packet should say to run npm install first

what: agent.context for 'list and stop the servers and tabs the engine started' returned only the shared rules and the art-and-assets lane. Nothing in the packet mentions bin/engine.mjs, vite.config.js or the dev server, so the packet cost tokens and answered nothing for a CLI task.
fix: add an engine/CLI lane keyed to bin/, engine/ and vite.config.js, and stop art matching a task with no art words

what: Starting the dev server rewrites tracked generated files a lane never touched — .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md and AGENTS.md — so a lane that starts a server for one proof must hand-revert files outside its own claim before it can commit.
fix: stop tracking the generated skill files, or write them only when the guide they come from has actually changed

what: The dev server binds to localhost, which resolves to IPv6 first on Windows, so anything probing it at http://127.0.0.1:<port> is refused and reads as 'no server running' while the server is healthy. Cost an hour of chasing a listing that said dead about a live server.
fix: listen on both loopback addresses, or say in the CLI help that the server answers on localhost only

what: The loop's clock cannot be set. makeLoop derives time from a private step count and exposes only reset(seed), which zeroes it, so a world restored after a hot reload comes back at time 0 while every entity sits where 5s of simulation left it — the snapshot then disagrees with itself and nothing but a sentence can explain why.
fix: Give makeLoop a way to resume a clock it did not run: reset(seed, { time }) or a setTime(seconds) that sets steps = round(seconds / STEP) without running a single step.

what: The committed .claude/skills/see-the-game/SKILL.md is generated from see.agent.md only at dev-server start, so it had drifted four commits behind the guide. The discovery layer a fresh agent actually reads was stale, and nothing said so — check passes, tests pass, and no server had run since the guide changed
fix: Regenerate the skill wherever the guide is read, not only at server start, and have engine.mjs check fail when a generated file does not match its source

what: see.capture and see.moment are unreachable headless, so the most state-mutating code in the See plugin has no automated coverage anywhere a lane can run. Both refuse at 'typeof document === undefined || !context.renderer', which is the FIRST line, so a restore probe headless only ever exercises that refusal. The camera borrow, the studio (hidden entities, nulled background and fog, dimmed lights, emptied post chain, added light rig), the ID silhouette pass and the readback crop are all browser-only, and a lane forbidden from opening a tab cannot prove any of them put the world back. I proved them by reading and by making the restore structural, which is weaker evidence than a green run.
fix: Give the headless world a null renderer that answers the same surface — scene with children, sync, draw, drawInto filling a buffer, passes.list/set, modelState — so the browser-only commands run their whole mutate-and-restore path with no GL. Frames would come back blank and the commands would still say so, but every finally would execute and a restore probe could prove them. engine/start-world-node.mjs is where it would attach.

what: The script op's simulate step always answers a full snapshot with every entity, so a probe that needs before-and-after state pays for a third copy it never asked for. engine/inspect.js simulate ends 'return api.snapshot({ entities: true, ...options })' — 60KB of the meadow's 761 entities per simulate, on every step of every script. My restore probe runs fifteen scripts each starting with a simulate, and the JSON I had to buffer and discard was several times the size of the answer I wanted.
fix: Let simulate answer the compact snapshot by default and take entities only when asked — simulate(seconds, {entities:true}) — or answer {time, counts} and let the caller add a snapshot step. Either way a script step should not decide for the caller what to return.

what: npm test drove the live editor and left two _probe_<pid> entities saved into kitten-survivors/levels/meadow.json. The CLI suite spawns probe entities against whichever editor answers, the editor persists them to the level file, and nothing removes them — so running the tests edits a game's authored level and the diff shows up as the project's own work
fix: The CLI suite must drive a world it owns, or destroy every entity it spawns in a finally; a test that writes to an authored level is a test that cannot be run twice

note: Gave makeLoop a resume({steps, seed, draws}) that is explicit and separate from reset, added loop.steps and random.draws, and made mulberry32 rejoinable by jumping its state to seed + n stream steps. A restored world now comes back at the same step count with the same next random numbers.

what: A plugin's own list of what it spawned cannot be rebuilt when the world is. Restoring a captured moment puts every entity back and emits entity:added for each, but a plugin that keeps its members in a private group — the crowd the horde drives is the live example — never re-adds them, so 33 restored enemies stood still while the same run simulated on without them. The kernel cannot know which group a restored entity belonged to.
fix: engine/reload-notice.js now emits world:restored after a restore. Have Spatial Hash and Crowd rebuild group membership from it, and say in the plugin guides that any plugin holding a list of entities must listen for it.

what: Nothing can add a field to snapshot() from outside inspect.js. makeInspect returns a closed object built at the very end of startWorld, so a fact the kernel learns during boot — the page was reloaded and the world rebuilt — can only reach an agent by monkey-patching engine.snapshot and engine.run after the fact. Wrapping a surface to say one true thing is the wrong shape for it.
fix: Let makeInspect take a list of contributors that snapshot() folds in, or give the returned surface a note(key, value) that snapshot reads and clears once.

what: A page reload the editor asks for itself is invisible to the page. Live File Updates calls location.reload() when a project plugin changes, and Vite fires vite:beforeFullReload only for reloads it decides on, so the one reload path the editor owns announced nothing at all — the file behind it had to be guessed from whichever engine:changed arrived in the two seconds before pagehide.
fix: Have hot.js emit a bus event naming the file before it calls location.reload(), so the reason travels with the reload instead of being inferred from timing.

note: simulate is compact by default now; 63KB a call became 328 bytes
same fix as p144 — simulate no longer dumps every entity per script step
loadPlugins takes the loader in both boot paths
the log is made right after the bus, so boot errors reach snapshot().errors
engine/plugin-import.js holds the one rule; both finders call it

Live File Updates now emits reload:before on the bus with the file that caused it, immediately before location.reload(). The reason travels with the reload instead of being guessed from whichever engine:changed arrived last, which was wrong exactly when a refactor touched two files at once.

what: A world restored from a captured moment can look exactly right and run wrong, and until now nothing stopped an agent running it. The entities come back in the right places but the crowd, pool or wave counter that drove them was rebuilt empty, so a simulate() after a restore quietly answers about a different game.
fix: Time is now held under the name restored-world whenever entities made during the run came back, so snapshot().paused says it on every reading, not just the first. Remove the hold once plugin membership can be rebuilt — see p158.

note: the sidecar carries marks now, and the guide says palette names outline colours and never a material colour
light is measured over drawn pixels; the studio rat went from mean 10 to mean 25 with measuredFraction 0.44
an alone studio frame is unmarked on purpose, ships no palette, and says so in the reply
the guide says simulating does not move the camera, and names see.view aim and the saved meadow-play view

what: A committed See frame, agent-runs/see/brief-on.json, was shot through a stale browser module after a hot reload and shows the OLD mark rule — twelve of twelve marks on scenery. Nothing on the artifact says which build made it, so it read as post-fix evidence and was cited as such in a findings table
fix: Stamp every sidecar with the commit and the mark-rule version that produced it, so a frame cannot be read as evidence for a build it predates

what: Two browser tabs answer one server, and nothing says which one replied. Consecutive commands landed on different tabs holding different worlds: snapshot reported 892 entities with 116 rats while see.describe and see.find, run seconds either side of it, saw 749 entities and no rats at all. An agent reading those two replies has no way to tell it asked two different worlds.
fix: Name the answering tab in every reply, and make servers warn when more than one tab is attached. A verb to close a tab by id would let a run pin exactly one.

what: A probe agent left snapshot.tmp.json and snapshot_output.txt in the repository root. The CLI gives no place to put a large reply, so an agent redirects it beside the code it is reading and the next agent.merge blocks on files nobody meant to keep.
fix: Name a scratch directory in help, or write large replies to one by default and print the path.

what: ENGINE_PROJECT is honoured by the dev server and ignored by check, so 'ENGINE_PROJECT=x node bin/engine.mjs check' silently reports on the default project instead of x. It answers ok with zero problems while the named project has six, and nothing in the reply names which project was read.
fix: Name the project in every check reply. Fail, or warn loudly, when ENGINE_PROJECT is set and --project is not.

what: A stray non-JS file in a project's types directory crashes the type loader with a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION stack trace on stdout, ahead of the JSON reply, so every command that loads types answers unparseable output. A .bak left beside a type file is enough.
fix: Load only .js from types, and report anything else as a named problem rather than importing it.

what: Plugin load warnings print to stdout ahead of the JSON reply, so any caller that parses the output fails. The Damage/Health name collision makes every default-project command unparseable, and a stray file in types/ does the same with a stack trace.
fix: Send every diagnostic to stderr and keep stdout to the reply alone.

what: Two dev servers both served kitten-survivors and the CLI bridge silently chose the other one. The refusal named a port but never said a second server existed, so the tab I had open looked broken
fix: when more than one dev server answers, name every one and which checkout it serves, not just the port the bridge picked

what: A changed plugin returned undefined over the bridge while the same code returned the right value headless. The browser was running a cached module and nothing said so
fix: have the bridge reply carry the module build id so a stale tab is named rather than silently answering with old code

what: The editor round-trip wrote a collider onto a level placement that only duplicated the type's own collider, which then showed up as a real diff in a generated file
fix: toLevel should not write a placement key that is identical to the type's

what: Re-running the meadow generator produced a 14292 to 753 line diff with identical content, because the committed file had been serialised by the editor and not by the generator. The tool's own header promises a reviewable diff
fix: either the editor writes a generated level in the generator's format, or check warns that a generated file was last written by the editor

what: A camera override for see.capture made it easy to measure a frame nobody plays. The spawn-clear circle gave numbers that no amount of art change could move, and nothing warned the frame was unrepresentative
fix: a verb that frames a representative play position, or a warning when a capture holds almost none of the level's own props

what: Every mesh cast a shadow and no placement could opt out. A flat ground decal is a thin box, so under a low key it threw a hard black rectangle of its own outline across the surface it was part of, and the frame filled with black quads nobody could account for
fix: done: mesh.shadow false casts nothing and still receives. Documented in lights.agent.md

what: A Blender script's hardcoded absolute path (as make-kitten-survivors-kitten.py uses) silently misses a worktree: BlenderMCP is one shared external process with normal OS file access, not scoped to any worktree, so exec(open(mainCheckoutPath)) reads/writes the main checkout while the agent's own files live only in its worktree until merge. Two failed exec calls before I found it.
fix: New Blender scripts read LIB_PATH and MODEL_PATH from globals().get(name, defaultMainCheckoutPath), so a caller running from a worktree can pre-set both before exec'ing the file, and the file still runs unmodified from the main checkout by default.

what: agent.release completed a lane while two of its three tests failed. tests.run exits 0 with failing tests, so the release gate passes anything that runs. The gate is the only automatic check on a parallel lane.

agent.release leaves the worktree and branch on disk; only agent.merge removes them. Preparing the same id again fails with 'worktree path already exists' and names no way out. A released lane that is not merged is an orphan nothing cleans.

agent.prepare --project kitten-survivors writes the lane packet to <workspace>/project/.engine/agent-task.json — the default project directory, not the one in use. A brief that points at the chosen project's .engine finds nothing.

note: the headless and live CLI paths now exit 1 when the answer reports a failure, so agent.release refuses a lane whose tests failed
the worktree-exists error now names agent.merge and the git commands that free the id
the packet is written beside the project in use and its path is returned as run.packet
engine.run awaits the command handler, so an async command answers its measurement instead of a pending promise

what: see.capture ignored its documented-looking file option and always wrote agent-runs/see/<name>.png, so a caller naming a path silently got a frame somewhere else.

note: see.capture honours file as the whole path, refuses one outside agent-runs, and the guide names both file and name

what: Combat Effects places a decal on every hit and every kill, but particles.art.blood and .bulletHole default to empty strings and Decals draws an untextured decal as a solid tinted quad. Any project that enables Combat Effects gets solid coloured squares on the ground by default, at the 300 cap within a minute, with no warning from check or from the plugin.

particles.effect(name, options) spreads the caller's options over the recipe, so particles.define cannot change any value the caller passes. Combat Effects passes count on every hit and kill, so a game restyling the builtin hit wiring can change its colours but never its counts — the documented tuning door does not reach the numbers that decide the particle budget.

A headless simulate stops advancing when Choice Screen opens and says so only as a paused array in the snapshot. simulate 150 silently returns at 22 seconds with no error, so a run script looks like it worked. Every lane measuring a late-game moment hits this and has to discover choice.pick by reading the builtin.

The effects ruling hit-is-the-brightest-thing checks value.p95 >= 0.85 over the whole frame, which no effect can move: a hundred particles a few pixels each cannot reach the 95th percentile of 233k pixels. Measured 0.613 with 81 particles live and 0.613 again with a 108-particle level-up fountain on screen — identical to three decimal places. The number is pinned to the brightest ground tone. A measured ruling filed under effects that only the world's floor can satisfy is unactionable by the lane that owns it.
see.capture drew only the GL canvas, so the HUD and every game screen were missing from every frame. The interface could not be seen, judged or compared, and nothing said the frame was incomplete.

note: see.capture composites the hud-layer and screen-layer canvases over the GL frame unless ui is false

what: engine/frame-facts.js boxesTouch uses strict <, so two boxes in exact contact report touching: false. see.describe between.touching asks a contact question of an overlap predicate: a kitten whose bottom face is exactly y=0 on a floor whose top face is exactly y=0 reads as not touching, and the see-battery test asserting 'the kitten stands on the ground, so their boxes touch' cannot pass however the level is authored.

A parallel lane was told to make two failing game tests pass, but kitten-survivors/tests belongs to another lane's claim. The see-ray test asserts the level's old defect as its expectation (floor six metres below the kitten); the level was fixed three rebuilds ago and the test was never updated. A test that encodes a defect and a claim boundary that forbids editing it leave the failure unfixable by anyone in the run.

kitten-survivors/levels/meadow.json is written by tools/make-kitten-survivors-meadow.mjs, but a lane claim can grant the level without granting tools/. The lane that owns the level must hand-edit it and the generator silently diverges: the next run of the generator drops the lane's work. A claim over a generated file should carry its generator.

see.capture refuses under --headless, so checking a frame against art.check needs a dev server and a live browser tab. In a worktree that also means --port, because plain 'run' drives the main workspace's editor and refuses. Four commands and a browser to answer 'is the frame bright enough'.

choice.pick takes a bare positional argument (run choice.pick 1) but its reply to an object argument is 'there is no NaN on this list', which names neither the right form nor the parameter. Every other run command in this engine takes a JSON object, so the first three attempts were wasted.

A frame could only be taken at the shape of the window the agent happened to have, so a game designed for a phone was judged on an ultra-wide desktop frame and every measured number belonged to the wrong picture.

note: see.capture takes size [width,height]; the renderer draws at that shape and the window's own size is put back after

what: Correction: p184 is NOT resolved. It was marked resolved by mistake with a note about see.capture size, which belongs to p189. p184 is the boxesTouch strict-comparison defect in engine/frame-facts.js and is still open.

note: see.capture takes size [width,height]; the renderer draws at that shape and the window's own size is put back after
boxesTouch compares with <= and a 0.1 mm tolerance, so exact contact counts as touching; the see-battery kitten-on-ground assertion passes

what: agent-runs/painpoints.jsonl is append-only and every parallel lane writes to it, so any cherry-pick or merge between lanes conflicts on the pain log itself. Recording friction creates friction.

note: gitattributes marks agent-runs/painpoints.jsonl merge=union, so parallel lanes' entries both survive a merge instead of conflicting

what: A GLB model ignores mesh.material, so the toon material's outline parameter cannot reach a creature: engine/render.js buildModel clones the file's own materials and never consults described.material. The only way to outline a model is to bake an inverted hull into the GLB. materials.agent.md says a material is named on a mesh and does not say that a model is the exception.

tools/blender/lib.py winds loft() so face normals point INTO the body while rounded_block() winds them outward, and nothing says so. Every model built from it exports with mixed normals, which only goes unnoticed because Blender exports doubleSided by default. Any effect that pushes along a normal — an inverted hull, a shell, an inflate — is half inside out until it recalculates first.

see.capture with subject and alone answers the studio frame from a fixed three-quarter angle, which is the worst angle for a flying enemy built as a flat-winged shape: the crow read as two planks in three-quarter and as a clean bird in shot:top. A judgement frame should default to the angle the game's own camera uses, or the guide should say to take shot:top for anything that flies.

engine.simulate(n) returns as if it ran n seconds when a named loop.hold is up. A choice screen holds the world, so every unattended simulation of this game stopped dead at the first level-up and reported the frozen moment as the answer. Two lanes lost time to it separately. simulate should report the seconds it actually advanced, or refuse while a hold is up.
fix: Return the seconds advanced from simulate/step, or name the holder

what: loop.holdFor (hit stop) skips onFixed entirely, so no system runs for those frames, while a named loop.hold runs every system with a step of zero. Two different meanings of 'held' with opposite effects on systems, and neither is visible from the outside. A test that simulated two steps after a kill saw nothing happen and read as a broken feature.

runClock.watch accepts an entity, and a level reload replaces every entity. Anything that watches a body instead of a lookup ends the next run at 0:00, and nothing warns. The retry in this game soft-locked on exactly that for the whole life of the feature. watch should keep a lookup, or say so when handed a body.
fix: Resolve to a lookup, or warn when given an entity

what: Screen repaints only inside a frame system, so after changing what a screen shows you must let a frame pass before see.capture or the capture answers with the PREVIOUS picture. A stale frame looks exactly like a real one, so it is only caught by noticing the numbers disagree. Cost me three captures. Screen could stamp the item-list key into the reply, or see.capture could wait a frame.

art.check measures the WHOLE frame, so an interface ruling like hud-is-bright is decided mostly by the world's pixels. At one moment the meadow alone measured value.p95 0.623 and the same moment with the HUD measured 0.672 — the interface is what carries the ruling, but nothing in the reply says so. see.capture already answers ui:false, so art.check could take the pair and report the interface's own contribution.

Editing any plugin under a running dev server reloads the page and puts the world back held under restored-world, so every one-line colour change on a HUD costs a full stop, play, start, simulate and re-pick cycle before the next frame can be taken. Eight cycles for this lane. A visual lane iterating on colours pays minutes per character.

A placement lying flat in the floor is swallowed by its own toon outline. meadow-prop carries outline 0.14; a 0.06 m thick water slab under it drew as a solid block of the outline colour, so a 26 m wide blue boundary read as cream. The inverted-hull outline should be capped at some fraction of the smallest box side, or a flat box should be exempt.

see.capture over the bridge returns the last painted frame when the editor tab is in the background, with no warning. see.identify refuses a hidden tab by name; capture answers with a stale picture that measures fine and is simply not the current world. Three rounds of art.check were spent on frames of a level that had already been replaced.

agent.merge takes the first registry entry with the id, so a run id reused from an earlier session matched that old merged record, returned already:true and silently skipped the merge. A finished lane reported as landed while its branch stayed unmerged.

note: agent.merge takes the newest registry entry with the id, so a reused id cannot match an older merged record

what: Hit stop and body collection interact invisibly: Health collects the dead in a fixed system, and a holdFor hit stop skips fixed systems, so a body killed at the moment of a hit is not collected inside the window a test simulates. wave-arc's corpse assertion fails on the merged build while a real run holds its cap exactly across 913 kills.

note: simulate reports asked, advanced and heldBy when a hold ate the time, so a held run cannot read as a full one

what: play:started is emitted before loop.start(), so context.loop.running is false inside a play:started handler. A plugin that wants to hold the world the moment play begins cannot tell it is playing, and a hold written as 'if (loop.running) loop.hold(...)' silently never takes. Kitten Survivors' title card ran the whole game underneath itself because of this.

Screen repaints only when its item list changes, and offers no way to ask for a repaint. A screen that draws from anything outside the item list — a copy of the world canvas, a texture, a measured layout — is painted once and can never refresh. Kitten Survivors' frosted menu had to carry a version number in its own item to force one.

The renderer makes its WebGL context without preserveDrawingBuffer, so the world canvas reads back empty once the browser has composited it. Anything that wants the drawn world outside a draw call — a menu blur, a thumbnail, a transition — must keep its own copy, and see.capture's 'canvas read back empty' error is the same fact. Neither render.agent.md nor see.agent.md says so.

A hidden browser tab runs zero frames — the loop's background setInterval is throttled to nothing — so see.capture returns the screen layer as it was last painted and a screen that has just changed is not in the picture. 'Let a frame pass' is not enough advice: with several lanes sharing one Chrome window every lane's tab but one is hidden, and no frame passes at all. see.capture should say so when document.hidden is true, the way it already reports an empty readback.

note: see.capture refuses a hidden tab when the interface is in the frame, and the guide says the tab must be in front
start-world names the ordering: play:started fires before the start hooks, so loop.running is false in a handler and gating on it does nothing

what: see.capture from a hidden browser tab answers with a frame whose particles and damage numbers are whatever was last drawn. The world is re-rendered, so entities look current and nothing says the effects layer is stale; every before/after measurement of an effect reads zero. Chrome gives a background tab no animation frame, and the particle painter and the number painter both run in the frame phase. Workaround: 'simulate 0.017' before each capture — under a hold it moves nothing and still runs the frame phase. see.capture should run one frame itself, or refuse.

Particles draw from the same seeded random stream as the simulation, so changing how many dots an effect emits changes where enemies spawn. Cutting brass from one dot to none and the muzzle flash from one to five moved three of seven game tests across their thresholds without touching a rule. A visual change should not be a gameplay change: give Particles its own stream off the same seed.

Damage Numbers cannot be told where a number starts. Its automatic entity:hurt listener calls a show() held inside its own onLoad closure, so wrapping context.damageNumbers.show never sees it, and defaults carries size, life, rise and drift but no lift. A game whose actors are a third of a metre gets every number 0.4 m above the hit point with no owner under it. Add defaults.lift, or have the listener call the published show.

Combat Effects places the muzzle flash 0.3 m along the fire direction from the shooter's own position. That is inside any actor under a metre, and a game cannot move it: particles.define restyles the recipe but the point comes from the call site. A weapon firing must never cover the thing that fired it. Take the reach from the weapon, or read it off the shooter's box.

kitten.pause toggles and takes no argument, so a script cannot ask for a held clock — it has to guess the current state. run.state.seconds is rounded to whole seconds, so it cannot be used to tell whether time is moving either; only snapshot.time can. A command that sets a state should take the state.

There is no verb for 'how much of this entity does an effect cover'. see.occlusion only names entities as blockers, and particles, decals and damage numbers are not entities, so the one thing that erases a player is invisible to it. Measuring it takes two captures of a held moment differenced inside the entity's own hull — see agent-runs/2026-08-31-brawl-stars/feel2/flash-cover.mjs. It belongs in See.

A held clock does not hold the picture. The game camera closes a sixth of the gap to its target on every frame, and simulate runs one frame per call however many steps it was asked for, so two captures of the same held moment can differ over 70% of an entity. Any pixel comparison has to settle the camera with repeated single-frame calls first, and prove it is still by capturing the same moment twice.

note: particles bind to context.drawing, a second seeded stream, so a change to an effect no longer moves where an enemy spawns
the corpse assertion drains the hit stop before asking what the fixed systems did, so it measures steps rather than seconds

what: Editing a plugin's .agent.md makes 'check' exit 1 and fails two offline tests, because the generated .claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md copy goes stale. The error names 'start the dev server' as the fix, but a server was already running and did not rewrite it. No guide names the one-line escape hatch.
fix: Say the exact command in the error: node -e "import('./engine/agent-registration.mjs').then(m => m.writeGeneratedAgentFiles(process.cwd(), '<project>'))" — or give it a CLI op, 'agent.regenerate'.

what: Five parallel lanes share one Chrome window and its renderer processes wedge under the load. A wedged tab is indistinguishable from a missing one: 'bridge.status' says only 'no editor attached', and every claude-in-chrome call times out after 45s. Three tabs died this way and each cost a full 30s arc to replay.
fix: Make bridge.status separate 'a tab is attached but has not drawn for N seconds' from 'no tab attached', and name the tab. 'servers' already knows which tabs are attached to a port — it should say when one has gone quiet.

what: There is no way to read renderer.stats from the CLI. Measuring what a rendering change costs per frame — draw calls, triangles — meant driving window.engine.renderer.stats through a browser automation tool, which is the exact 'never read the page to see the game' route the base instructions forbid. The stats object exists and says it is there to be measured against.
fix: Add a 'render.stats' command beside 'materials.list' that answers context.renderer.stats, so 'run render.stats' works over the bridge.

what: servers.stop with no port kills every lane's dev server, including live ones. Mine was stopped mid-measurement by something outside this lane; the CLI answered 'no editor attached', which reads as a browser fault, and it cost a restart plus a replayed 30s arc to find out the server was gone.
fix: Make servers.stop with no port refuse while another checkout's server is running, or at least name whose it is stopping. 'no editor attached' should say when the port has no server at all — that is a different fault from a tab that is not open.

what: see.capture never wrote its file for subject+alone yet reported success, and art.check then measured the PNG left on disk from the previous capture and returned numbers identical to three decimals. A measurement command must refuse a frame older than the run that asked for it.
Every bridge error says 'Open http://localhost:5180' whatever --port was passed. Five parallel lanes each run their own port and the message sends all of them to one lane's server.

The Chrome MCP navigate tool with no tabId retargets the first tab in the shared group, which in a five-lane run belongs to another lane. I took another lane's tab and another lane took mine. A lane needs a tab it owns.

kitten.arc takes positional args as an array. Passing the documented-looking object '{"seconds":30}' is accepted silently and the default 120 is used instead. A command that cannot read its arguments should say so.

note: agent.skills rewrites the generated files from the CLI, and the stale-file errors name that command instead of a function
renderStats answers draw calls and triangles from the CLI, so measuring a rendering change needs no browser automation
servers.stop refuses a bare sweep while more than one server runs, names the ports, and takes 'all' when a sweep is meant
kitten.arc takes the object form and refuses an unknown key instead of playing the default
the bridge names its own server's port in the no-editor error
a reply carrying an error field exits non-zero, so a script cannot run its next step against the file the last one failed to write

what: A directional light's shadow camera is sized by `range` around the light entity and the map is fixed at 1024 texels, so no single fixed light can shadow a 90 m arena: range 47 covers 23.5 m and draws everything past it as shadowed, range 64 and 96 put 6 to 9 cm on a texel and the ground self-shadows into diagonal acne. Measured on kitten-survivors/meadow: shadow on gave edgeDensity 0.048 against a cap of 0.045, shadow off gave 0.017. The meadow now casts no shadow at all. It needs either a larger shadow map or a shadow camera that follows the player.

`run kitten.arc '{"seconds":30}'` silently plays 120 seconds. The command takes a positional array — `'[30, 15]'` — and an object argument is dropped without a word, so the run is four times longer than asked and every measurement is taken at the wrong moment. A command should refuse an argument shape it does not read.

When a level wedges the browser renderer, every engine command answers 'no editor attached. Open http://localhost:5180 and leave the tab open.' The tab is open and registered; the renderer is hung, and CDP Runtime.evaluate times out on it too. The message sends an agent to check the tab and the port instead of the level it just loaded. Reloading the page while `play` is running wedges it reliably, and a fresh tab is the only recovery.
A git worktree has no node_modules and nothing says so. npm run dev fails with a vite-not-found error that names no cause; every lane pays an install and a confused minute before its first command.

renderStats cannot be compared across a hot reload. A reload restores the world, so merged, keylines and contactShadows all reset and the camera moves, and an A/B of one render change reads as noise. There is no way to freeze a scene and toggle one renderer setting from the CLI.

The renderer has no idea which entity is the player. engine/render.js gets (canvas, view, viewport) and the camera plugin keeps its target private, so any render feature that marks the player needs a game file to name it. Game Camera now publishes view.follows; before that the only route was a game noun in the kernel.

A lane's claim lists the files it may write, but nothing stops it writing outside that list — the world-marks lane edited plugins/builtin/camera.js, which it did not claim. Claim Guard refuses a file another RUN claimed, so an unclaimed file is open to every lane at once.

see.view '{"aim":"you"}' aims the live camera and the level's camera follow rule never comes back. stop and play do not restore it, so every later see.describe, see.isolate and see.capture answers from a camera that is not the game's — a capture taken after an aim shows the editor's idle view while the run is live. Only a page reload puts the follow back. Either restore the level's camera block on play, or give see.view a way to hand the camera back.

Two ways to scale a model and neither is complete. A TYPE's scale key is dropped: engine/world.js builds an entity with scale: placement.scale ?? 1, so only a placement can scale. The alternative, mesh.scale, is applied by render.js sync (entity.scale * declared.scale) but NOT by drawSize or anchorOffset, both of which read mesh.box and entity.scale only. So a type drawn at mesh.scale 2 is reported by every See query at half its drawn size and its feet anchor is placed for the smaller box, unless the author restates mesh.box by hand at the grown size. Either read the type's scale in world.js, or fold declared.scale into drawSize and anchorOffset.

One Chrome serves every parallel lane, so the browser is the bottleneck of the whole parallel design: only the front tab draws, tabs wedge under load, navigate with no tabId retargets another lane's tab, and a wedged tab is indistinguishable from a missing one. Five lanes plus the coordinator contend for one renderer, and every visual measurement queues behind it. This is now the largest single source of lost lane time.

note: drawSize, anchorOffset and the draw all use one totalScale, so a mesh.scale model reports the size it is drawn at
see.view aim returns the camera it replaced and names the command that puts it back

what: A build-time value guard cannot compare a tint to a texture. A flat tint draws about half again brighter than a texture of the same measured value under the same light, so a generator that holds props within a band of the floor texture's mean puts them a third too light on screen. Nothing in the engine reports what a surface will DRAW at; every generator has to calibrate against a captured frame by hand.

art.check on a play frame measures whatever effect happens to be firing, not the world. The loop 2 baseline cleared bright-day at value.p95 0.996 because a hairball burst covered a fifth of the capture; the same level with no burst reads 0.553 and fails. subject:world does not exclude particles, so a ruling can pass or fail on the timing of a capture. A world-only mode, or a p95 taken over non-additive pixels, would make the number mean something.

The toon material makes light intensity a staircase, and nothing says so. steps:4 quantises the diffuse term, so raising a key from 6.2 to 7.4 moved the floor's drawn value by 0.02 and 7.4 to 8.0 moved it by 0.13. An agent tuning a light against a measured ruling reads the small step as no effect and gives up, or overshoots a whole band. materials.agent.md should state that steps quantises before the value is read.
A generator wrote its output and only then checked it, so a failed build guard exited non-zero with the rejected level already on disk. The next command read it as if it had passed.
A prop's centre and its box height were rounded apart, so a prop could sit half a rounding step under the floor and draw a cut line across the ground.

play writes the level file. A lane whose claim is five type files ends up with a 39,700-line diff on levels/meadow.json from running the command its own packet names, and the editor reformats one-line entities into expanded JSON so the diff cannot be merged. Restoring it needs git show HEAD:path > path, because git checkout is blocked.
fix: write only the camera block back on play, in the file's existing formatting

what: see.describe with brief:true lists ONLY marked entities, and marks are a fixed budget dealt by type — so counting a crowd with brief silently tops out at the budget. I measured 8 on screen for three different builds before noticing. The reply says listedOnlyMarked, but counts.visible is the honest number and nothing routes you to it. counts should carry visibleByType.

see.describe visible entities include bodies that are dead and lingering, and they carry the live type. A count of enemies on screen was 40% corpses. There is no way to ask for the living, so every caller has to cross the list against the game's own roster.

The saved play view meadow-play is a FIXED camera at the origin, but the level's camera is a chase camera. Any see query through that view measures a kitten that has run out of it. There is no verb for 'the camera this level would be using right now' — every measurement has to rebuild the chase camera from camera.rule by hand. see.view should take {rule:true} or the play camera should be reconstructible.

The CLI appends a libuv line to its own output on Windows after see.capture and art.check: 'Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src/win/async.c, line 94'. It lands after the JSON, so piping the output into JSON.parse fails and every caller has to hunt for the line starting with a brace.
fix: close the bridge handle once before exit

what: A headless loop that simulates until a clock reaches a target spins forever once anything holds the loop — a game-over screen, a queue of level-ups. simulate() returning without advancing is indistinguishable from a slow frame. simulate should answer how much clock it actually moved.

Parallel lanes contend for one foreground Chrome tab. A tab put in the background stops answering the bridge and every CLI call returns 'no editor attached' forever; reloading does not help and the only cure found was closing the tab and opening a new one. Four lanes cost about twenty minutes of this. servers does not say which tab is in front.
fix: servers should name the foreground tab, and the no-editor message should say the tab may be backgrounded rather than closed

what: npm run dev started from a bash subshell dies when the shell exits, and vite then reports 'port already in use' while the port answers 502 through the proxy. Nothing in the docs says how to hold a dev server up across CLI calls in a worktree.

Another lane's cleanup killed this lane's dev server mid-task. The help says a port answering for somebody else's checkout is named and never stopped, but the server on 5195 was stopped from outside this worktree and the restart came up on 5196, which broke every command line already written down.
fix: refuse to stop a server whose checkout is not the caller's, and say so

what: A model's colour cannot be measured from the engine. mesh.tint only paints the box that stands in while a GLB loads, so the only way to know what a family draws at is to read the Blender script that built it or to sample pixels out of a capture by hand. Every value ruling in art/world is stated in Rec.709 luminance and nothing in the engine reports it for a model.
fix: see.describe or a materials command should report a model's area-weighted material luminance, read from the GLB

what: Resuming a lane after agent.merge has removed its worktree drops it into the MAIN checkout with no warning: it keeps working, and its edits land in the shared tree beside the coordinator's. Nothing in the reply or the environment says the workspace it was given no longer exists.

note: saveLevel refuses while the loop is running, so pressing play cannot rewrite a generated level in the editor's formatting

what: A saved view named for a level's play camera goes stale the moment the level uses a chase camera, and nothing says so. meadow-play frames a kitten at the origin 12.75% from the top of the picture; the level's own rule frames it at 51.8%. Two tests and every human-facing frame count through the stale one. see.view should be able to save a RULE rather than a fixed eye, or see.describe should take {camera:'rule'}.

Tuning a seeded simulation one variable at a time is measuring noise. Changing a spawn distance changes the random stream, so two configurations are two seeds: a middle ring read 25 alive standing and died at 0:34 kiting, while both its neighbours survived past 2:00. There is no way to run the same level over N seeds and get a distribution, so every tuning claim in this project rests on one sample.

A measured art ruling written with only a minimum passes a frame that is blown past white. The references carry both ends — median 0.439 to 0.821, p95 0.661 to 0.927 — and the generated rulings kept only the low one, so a key light raised to reach the minimum sailed past every reference with nothing objecting.

The keyline silently covers the families it is most needed on. hullGeometry drops any mesh whose signed volume is negative, to exclude a modelled inverted hull — but the creature models are built by tools/blender/lib.py loft(), which winds inward, so a whole body can be dropped and the entity draws with no keyline while renderStats still counts it. A flat open mesh such as a wing has no signed volume at all and cannot be hulled this way in either winding: grown along its normals and drawn back-side it paints one face solid. Three blind critic rounds have reported no outlines on enemies while the counter read 82.

note: Mis-filed: I passed a JSON object and pain stored it as prose. Re-logged correctly as the next id.

what: The run registry disagrees with git and nothing reconciles the two. All five loop-3 lane branches are ancestors of HEAD, so every one is merged; the registry records props3, world-marks, see-ray and see-identity as complete and render-kit as blocked. Status is written by whichever verb ran last and is never checked against the branch. An agent reading agent.status to decide what still needs merging gets the wrong answer for all five, and the safe reading -- merge it again -- is the one that wastes a lane.
fix: agent.status should derive state from git rather than replay the last write: for each run report whether its branch is an ancestor of HEAD, whether git still lists its worktree, and whether its directory is on disk. Registry status becomes a hint; git becomes the truth.

what: Merged lanes keep their worktrees and removed worktrees keep their directories. After loop 3, .agent-worktrees holds five directories: props3 and world-marks are still linked git worktrees at 59 MB and 110 MB although both branches are in HEAD, and render-kit, see-identity and see-ray are directories with no .git left behind by a worktree that was removed. Nothing reports either state. Grepping the engine from the repo root now matches four stale copies of agent-registration.mjs, so a search over the workspace returns hits from code that is not the code that runs.
fix: agent.merge should remove the worktree it merged, and a cleanup verb should list directories in .agent-worktrees that git does not list as worktrees and offer to delete them. Add .agent-worktrees to the ignore list used by index and by the repo grep guidance.

what: The run registry keys runs by an id that is not unique. arena and creatures each appear twice with different outcomes -- one merged, one blocked -- because a second lane reused the name after the first finished. agent.merge took the first match and reported success without merging anything until it was changed to take the newest. Every other lookup in the file still takes the first or any match.
fix: agent.prepare should refuse an id that an unmerged run already holds, and suggest a free one. Runs that are finished may share a name safely, but two live lanes with one id cannot be told apart by any verb that takes an id.

what: agent.status prints the whole registry raw. Thirty-nine runs, each carrying its full check output including captured test logs, so the one question it is asked -- which lanes are live and which files are claimed -- is buried in tens of thousands of tokens. Reading it costs more than the coordination it is supposed to save, so agents skip it and collide instead.
fix: Default agent.status to live runs only, one line each: id, derived state, claimed files, worktree present. Put the full record behind --all or --id <name>. Check output belongs in the run's own directory, not inline in a registry every reader must parse.

what: pain is the one verb that takes prose and flags while every other verb in this CLI takes one JSON object. Passing pain a JSON object does not fail -- it stores the whole object as the prose of the painpoint and exits 0, so the record looks written and is garbage. I did this and had to resolve a false record to undo it.
fix: Either accept a JSON object as pain does for every other verb, or refuse a first argument that parses as JSON and print the flag form. Silently storing it is the only bad option.

what: The CLI accepts a project name with a trailing space and silently creates a directory for it. Running the CLI suite left an untracked directory named 'kitten-survivors ' at the repo root holding a generated .engine index, beside the real kitten-survivors. Nothing warns, and on Windows a trailing-space directory is awkward to remove by hand. The same run reported no level named with an em dash, so an unparsed argument reached --project as a value.
fix: Trim the --project value and refuse a name that is not a directory already in the checkout, rather than creating one. A project is opened, never created by a flag.

note: agent.status now derives state from git: agentState reports landed (branch is an ancestor of HEAD), branchExists, hasWorktree and onDisk, and flags any run git says landed that the registry does not. Root cause was mergeAgent updating the registry after cleanup, so a worktree removal that failed threw before the merge was recorded.

agent.merge now records the merge before cleanup and reports a removal it could not do, and agent.sweep removes worktrees and orphan directories whose work is in HEAD plus any landed branch left behind. Swept the five real leftovers; 169 MB reclaimed and .agent-worktrees is empty.

agent.prepare refuses an id held by a run that is not merged and suggests a free one. mergeAgent matches its own record on id plus startedAt, so a reused id stamps the run that was merged rather than the first with that name.
agent.status defaults to live runs, lanes still to merge, records git says already landed, and leftovers on disk. The raw registry moved behind --all.

what: Captures default to the browser window size, so art is judged at whatever shape the tab happens to be. The art bibles state a portrait phone, 390 pt wide, 1080 px short edge, and the default viewport is 1280x720 landscape. Frames from one loop measure 1107x748, 540x960 and 1920x911, and the blind critic was shown a 540x960 portrait frame beside a 1920x911 landscape one in the same set. Frame shape changes how much arena is on screen, so every measured ruling and every A/B judgement is taken against an uncontrolled variable.
fix: A game declares its target device profile once -- viewport, device pixel ratio, orientation -- and see.capture and art.check use it unless a caller states another. A frame should carry the profile it was taken at, and a comparison set should refuse to mix profiles.

what: A project directory whose name ends in a space is unreachable by every Windows tool that made it. ENGINE_PROJECT picked up a trailing space from a cmd /c set VAR=value && ... launch, and the server then created 'kitten-survivors ' beside the real project and served the empty one: the editor showed 'level is empty' and snapshot reported project 'kitten-survivors '. Windows strips a trailing space when resolving a path, so git enumerated the real project's files through the bad name and then failed to open any of them, and rm on the bad name would have hit the real directory. Removing it needed a literal \?\ path.
fix: Trim ENGINE_PROJECT and refuse a name that is not already a directory in the checkout. A project is opened, never created by a flag, so a name that does not resolve should fail at start-up with the list of directories that do.

what: A headless browser started for a lane outlives the process that started it. tools/hold-headless-editor.mjs kills Chrome on SIGTERM and SIGINT, and neither arrives when the holder is killed from a Git Bash pkill on Windows, so Chrome keeps running with its temp profile and nothing records that it exists. Seven were running against one server when three were wanted. A leaked headless browser is invisible: it has no window, it does not appear in the servers registry, and the only way to find one is to read Win32_Process command lines for --user-data-dir.
fix: Record a lane browser the way a dev server is recorded -- port, pid, client name, profile directory, the checkout it serves -- and give it the same lifecycle: a list verb that proves each entry by asking its debugging port, and a stop verb. A holder should also exit when its parent does, so an orphan cannot outlive the run that made it.

note: The libuv assertion is a real process abort, not cosmetic noise, and the cause is fetch: it keeps its connection in a pool the caller cannot close, and a socket still closing when process.exit runs aborts node on Windows with the assertion printed after the command's own output. A liveness probe now uses node:http with agent:false and destroys its own socket, and lanes exits 0 clean. Any CLI path that fetches and then forces an exit can hit this; node:http is the fix, not a delay.

Lane browsers are recorded in project/.engine/lane-browsers.json with client name, port, pid, profile directory and checkout. lanes lists them and proves each against its own debugging port, lanes.start adds one, lanes.stop ends one or all and deletes the profile. Started detached with stdio ignore so a browser outlives the command that started it, the way a dev server does.

what: A headless lane browser rewrote the project's level file. Driving play and then stop through a lane client saved kitten-survivors/levels/meadow.json back to disk, expanding a deliberately compact generated file from 1264 lines to 23413 and reordering its camera keys. The level says GENERATED at the top and is rebuilt by a tool, so any save from a client destroys the authored formatting; worse, a lane exists to be isolated and it wrote to the shared checkout. saveLevel already refuses while the loop is running, which does not cover the save that stop performs.
fix: A client should declare itself a viewer or a driver, and only a driver may write. A lane render client is a viewer: it plays, simulates and captures, and every write path -- save on stop included -- is refused for it. Separately a level that declares itself generated should refuse an editor save outright and say which tool rebuilds it.
